boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Fort Ridgely record (August 20-22, 1862) in Operations to Suppress the Sioux Uprising [August-September 1862]. Captain Marsh's ambush on the way to the Lower Sioux Agency before the attacks, the killings of settlers across the Minnesota River Valley and the refugees' arrival are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the Fort Ridgely garrison and refugee civilians and the Santee Sioux without figures; the live field reads 0. The frozen description gives about 400 Sioux on August 20 and 800 on August 22. Sheehan names the remnant of Company B and a detachment of Company C of the Fifth Minnesota and the newly organized Renville Rangers as his only troops, with armed refugees aiding the defense, and gives no figures; he describes a large force on the 20th and a much larger one on the 22nd, and Jones a very large force.
claims.rationale: Unit names and qualitative descriptions only; the frozen 400 and 800 are not traced in the inspected reports. No account by the Dakota side was inspected; every statement of their numbers, aims and losses comes from their opponents or from the NPS summary. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are First Lieutenant Timothy J. Sheehan and Little Crow (no rank recorded); the live page tags Little Crow [CS], which is not adopted. Sheehan signs as commanding the post and ordered the outbuildings destroyed; the artillery was under Ordnance Sergeant Jones, and the Renville Rangers under Lieutenant Gorman. Jones credits Sheehan with organizing the casting of balls. The inspected reports do not name Little Crow; only NPS places the Santee under him.
claims.rationale: Command roles from two garrison reports and the NPS summary; no automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads US 16 and Indian losses unknown; the live field reads 26 (US 26; CS 0). Sheehan's return of casualties in the garrison for August 20 and 22 totals 16 (read as '3 13 16' in the garbled OCR columns, apparently 3 killed and 13 wounded). No inspected source gives a Dakota loss.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The return covers the garrison, not the armed refugees; the live 26 is not traced; the column reading is tentative.

open_questions: Marsh's August 18 ambush, the civilian refugees' numbers, the sources of the frozen 400 and 800, the names list Jones appended (not printed in the OCR), any Dakota account, histories of the war (Heard 1863 and others) and maps remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Sheehan's and Jones's August 26, 1862 reports are interested garrison accounts written the same day; Jones reports to Sheehan, but each is a separate author family. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.

No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Participants are named as the sources name them; characterizations in the sources (including 'hostile', 'savages', 'massacre' or 'battle') are quoted as the sources' own words and not adopted.
